title: Reboot: pre-unlock background launch makes DB open fail for the whole process
description: After reboot, the first app open showed 'StrapLog could not start' (sqlite read error); the second open worked (fault test 261017-0957-FAULT_TEST, 2026-10-17). Likely cause: CoreBluetooth restoration relaunches the app in the background before first unlock. Data protection (default completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication) makes live.sqlite unreadable then. AppDelegate.init builds AppDependencies once into a Result, so the failure sticks for the life of the process, and the user's tap brings that same failed process to the foreground. Also, AppDependencies opens the DB before PolarHeartSource, so the restore-id central manager is never created on that launch. Fix: create the HeartSource unconditionally in init; open the DB/model once protected data is available (isProtectedDataAvailable / applicationProtectedDataDidBecomeAvailable), and retry on foreground.

title: Watch shows H10 HR from BLE advertisements when the phone is unreachable
description:
When the iPhone is away or StrapLog is not running, StrapLogWatch should still show current H10 HR, display-only (no recording; the phone stays the only recorder).

Verified 2026-10-18 against Polar BLE SDK 8.4.0 (build/dd/SourcePackages/checkouts/polar-ble-sdk): documentation/products/PolarH10.md lists 'Heart rate broadcast'; the SDK reads it in startListenForPolarHrBroadcasts by scanning, never connecting.

Why advertisements: no BLE connection, so neither of the H10's two connection slots is used and the phone's link is undisturbed; no Settings pairing, so HealthKit keeps the Watch's optical HR.

Decoding (port of iOSCommunications BleAdvertisementContent.processManufacturerData + BlePolarHrAdvertisement): CBAdvertisementDataManufacturerDataKey, first 2 bytes LE company id 0x006B; content = rest. Content length 3 or 4 -> HR block directly. Otherwise walk blocks: if content[offset] & 0x40 == 0 it is an HR block (3 bytes; parser hands the remainder from offset), else skip content[offset+1]+2. HR block: byte0 bit0 battery, bit1 sensor contact, bits2-4 frame counter (new reading when it changes); displayed HR = slowAverageHr = byte3 if block length 4 else byte2.

Design: pure decoder in StrapLogCore (macOS-testable, fixture bytes from the SDK's own example 6b 00 72 06 7f 44 37 00 00 00 33 00 3c plus captured H10 bytes); a CoreBluetooth scanner in StrapLogWatch (no PolarBleSdk on watchOS); filter by the remembered H10 device id; Watch screen falls back to broadcast HR, clearly labelled, when WatchConnectivity says the phone is unreachable or LiveStatus is stale.

Limits: HR only (~1 Hz), no RR, so no RMSSD/alpha1; foreground only (no workout session; not for sleep).
design:
Failover (agreed 2026-10-18): phone first, strap only when the phone has no fresh HR.

- Pure HeartRateSourcePolicy in StrapLogCore -> .phone / .strap / .idle, from (phone status freshness, WCSession reachability, app foreground). Unit-tested with FakeClock.
- Phone detection is event-driven, no polling: LiveStatus pushes (LiveStatusThrottle, routine <=10 s, urgent at once) + WCSessionDelegate sessionReachabilityDidChange. PhoneLink.isStale / staleCheckInterval (5 s) already exist; reuse.
- .strap when foreground AND (phone unreachable -> immediately, OR phone status nil/not recording, OR stale ~15-20 s as backstop for reachable-but-silent).
- Back to .phone on the first fresh LiveStatus (not on reachability alone) -> hysteresis, no flapping at range edge. Stop scan at once.
- .idle (scan stopped) whenever scenePhase != .active; watchOS suspends on wrist-down anyway.
- Scanner: CoreBluetooth, AllowDuplicates true (needed for ~1 Hz), drop all but the remembered H10 id. The only costly piece; runs only wrist-up with no phone.
- Watch app just starts/stops the scanner per policy output; no logic in views.

Open questions to settle FIRST (spike on device before any design):

2. Capacity: how many hours of RR fit (overnight needs ~8-9 h). The sensor holds one recording at a time.
3. Timing: what timestamps the fetched exercise carries, and how to line them up with phone beats (rr1024 sums vs epoch ms) without double-counting overlaps (DuplicateHeartFilter).
4. Does a running internal recording change battery life or interfere with live streaming?

If (1) is HR-only, close as won't-do or reduce to HR gap-fill.

title: StandBy nightstand display of live HR/HRV via Live Activity
description:
Rik wants to set the iPhone on the nightstand in StandBy mode (charging, landscape, locked) and glance at live HR, RMSSD, DFA a1 etc. all night.

Feasibility: StandBy only shows WidgetKit widgets and Live Activities. Widgets are timeline-budgeted (a few reloads per hour), so they can't show live data. A Live Activity can: the app already stays alive in the background via bluetooth-central, and ActivityKit allows local updates from a running app, so RecordingSession can push its metrics. In StandBy a tapped Live Activity goes full-screen, and Night Mode tints it red automatically.

Work: Widget extension target in project.yml with ActivityAttributes and a ContentState (HR, RMSSD, a1, battery, elapsed); NSSupportsLiveActivities in Info.plist; start/stop the activity with recording in Launcher/RecorderModel through an abstraction (keep ActivityKit out of the packages); throttle updates to about 1 per 5-15 s; a StandBy/lock-screen layout with large numerals. Watch the 8 h Live Activity limit (12 h total on the lock screen) for overnight sessions; restarting the activity may be needed.

Acceptance: during an overnight recording, the phone in StandBy shows current HR/HRV that updates within about 15 s, and the activity ends when recording stops.

StandBy still opens on the minimal pill; one tap goes full screen (system behaviour, not settable). 8 h limit: ActivityKit refuses background starts, so a system-ended activity only comes back when the app is foregrounded (existing retry); with no push server this can't be avoided. A 22:30 start ends about 06:30. TO CLOSE: overnight StandBy shows large HR/α1, updates within 15 s, ends on Stop.
